input: RSA finding: S Tacoma Way corridor (S 47th-St to S 62nd-St) framed around Safe System shared responsibility. Task: state the responsibility principle.
output: Road safety is shared between those who design, build, operate, and use the system; strengthen every part so one failure does not kill.

input: RSA finding: community fears medians/lane loss for future BRT; dealerships park on planting strips. Task: recommend treatment.
output: Work with dealerships to end planting-strip parking; design medians to preserve BRT envelope; document access impacts before approval.

input: RSA finding: memo based on limited data with further analysis required before implementation. Task: state the caveat for decision-makers.
output: Recommendations rest on limited data at time of preparation; require further engineering analysis and design before implementation.

input: RSA finding: walking audit plus crash-mode/severity analysis 2017-2023. Task: rank corridor risk.
output: Rank by crash mode/severity concentration along S Tacoma Way segment and intersections; weight pedestrian-involved and severe crashes highest.

input: RSA finding: private vehicles enter transit-only center despite entrance signage. Task: recommend treatment.
output: Install more conspicuous Do Not Enter / Authorized Vehicles Only signs: larger, repositioned for turning-movement sight lines at each entrance.

input: RSA finding: drivers miss Road Closed sign at Pennington/Toole, loop through transit center to turn around. Task: recommend treatment.
output: Advance the Road Closed signing beyond decision point considering bus turning dimensions; add channelization so through-drivers cannot enter the loop.

input: RSA finding: on-street parking blocks streetcar when vehicles park improperly. Task: recommend treatment.
output: Remove parking along Congress Street and/or Broadway segments conflicting with streetcar swept path; repurpose for expanded sidewalks or public space.

input: RSA finding: long signal cycles penalize pedestrians at transit center. Task: recommend treatment.
output: Shorten cycle length to cut pedestrian delay and non-compliance risk, checking transit-vehicle progression impacts.

input: RSA finding: transit-access RSA covering vehicles, pedestrians, streetcar, parking, signals. Task: what prompt list applies?
output: Transit-access prompts: unauthorized entry compliance, stop/shelter access paths, parking vs transit-vehicle conflicts, signal timing for pedestrians, wayfinding to bays.

input: RSA finding: full-day workshop plus walking audit produced treatment list. Task: name minimum RSA team inputs for a corridor memo.
output: Crash data analysis, field walking audit, stakeholder workshop, speed/volume studies, and a Safe System framing section.

input: RSA finding: transit-center issues span signage, closures, parking, signals. Task: rank by implementation speed.
output: 1) Sign conspicuity upgrades (days). 2) Signal retiming (weeks). 3) Parking removal (months, needs approvals). 4) Geometric changes (capital program).

input: RSA finding: dealership parking on planting strips vs BRT median needs. Task: state the curb-space priority rule.
output: Safety and transit envelope outrank private parking on public planting strips; enforce, then design medians around the BRT path.

input: RSA finding: streetcar blocked by improper parking on some blocks only. Task: state the targeted (non-corridor-wide) fix.
output: Restrict parking only on blocks where swept-path analysis shows streetcar interference; keep compliant blocks parked.

input: RSA finding: transit-center loop misused as turnaround. Task: state the geometric fix when signs fail.
output: When sign upgrades do not stop loop misuse, channelize the entrance throat so through-vehicles physically cannot enter while buses can.
